lines.say: There's a reason
this young painter dared to look like Christ.
This is the Self-Portrait at Twenty-Eight,
painted by Albrecht Dürer in 1500.
Most people see it as stunning arrogance,
or even blasphemy.
His frontal pose,
his gaze and his blessing
hand all copy pictures of Christ.
And the picture seems to agree.
His long hair
and his calm eyes look straight out at you.
But look at his hair.
He painted it brown,
not his real reddish blond.
According to a later woodcut by Sebald Beham,
this exact face became the face of Christ.
In the next century,
Johann Georg Vischer used it for Christ again.
It isn't Dürer pretending to be Christ.
It's Christ who ended up wearing Dürer's face.
So did he copy Christ,
or did Christ end up copying him?
